selected_subject.org: University of Alaska System (Office of Information Technology)
selected_subject.anchorage_tie: Bowl-impact tie, not residency. Shier is a former UAA Chief Information Officer; the draft policy he presented would require every UA campus, including the University of Alaska Anchorage, to adopt an AI plan for its students, faculty and staff. UA System OIT is based in Fairbanks and the September regents meeting was held at UAS in Juneau.

subject_quotes.verbatim: How do you ensure data privacy and protection? How do you provide monitoring?
subject_quotes.context: Shier framing the governance questions the draft AI policy addresses, in his presentation to the UA Board of Regents.

selected_decision.what_happened: University of Alaska leadership presented a draft artificial intelligence policy to the Board of Regents. If approved, it would require all three campuses to have an AI plan in place for students, faculty and staff. The guiding principles in the draft emphasize not replacing human talent, maintaining data security and leveraging AI to improve access to education services. Ben Shier, the university's Chief Information Technology Officer, presented it; he said the draft came together over the summer without enough faculty and student feedback, and that the university currently can't control and track every usage of AI. Leadership plans to submit a finalized draft for approval at the November regents meeting, after fall student listening sessions and online surveys (no dates scheduled as of Sept 16).
selected_decision.when_note: Date of first report (KTOO, Wednesday Sept 16, 2026) on the September regents meeting held at UAS in Juneau; exact meeting day not published in fetched sources. Inside the 60-day window either way.

corroborating_sources.outlet: Alaska Public Media (syndicated KTOO story, Jamie Diep)
corroborating_sources.note: Same reporter/story syndicated statewide; independent of UA but not a separate reporting line. Adds the detail that the draft came together over summer without enough faculty/student feedback.

corroborating_sources.outlet: University of Alaska OIT, Generative AI Security Standard
corroborating_sources.note: Subject-org document. Confirms the existing mandatory Generative AI Security Standard (effective Jan 2025, revised Mar 2025, owner OIT Information Security and Assurance, supplements Regents Policy R02.07): Internal and Restricted data (FERPA, HIPAA) may not be used with unapproved generative AI tools.

selected_decision.the_binary: Adopt a top-down, system-wide AI governance framework that obligates every campus (including UAA) to produce an AI plan, versus leaving AI adoption to campus, department and faculty discretion under the existing OIT data-security standard.
selected_decision.ak_consequence: Higher education and workforce: a system-wide AI framework binding UAA, UAF and UAS students, faculty and staff, layered on the existing OIT Generative AI Security Standard; approval vote targeted for the November 2026 Board of Regents meeting.
selected_decision.debatable_axis: Pro: a principled framework (human talent, data security, access) sets guardrails before AI use sprawls further; 85% of college students use generative AI in coursework per a 2025 Inside Higher Ed survey cited by KTOO. Con: Shier himself says the draft lacked faculty and student input and the university can't track all AI use, so the Nov. vote risks adopting principles ahead of enforcement capacity.

context_facts: A 2025 Inside Higher Ed survey found about 85% of college students use generative AI in coursework (cited by KTOO).
Regent Christine Ressler raised concerns about data security capabilities (KTOO).
UA provides online guidance on data security; OIT Generative AI Security Standard effective Jan 2025, revised Mar 2025.
structural_read: Governance before scale is the right sequencing, and the three principles are defensible anchors. The honest gap is process: the draft was assembled over summer without faculty and student input and lacks tracking capacity, so the November vote is where it becomes either governance with implementation behind it or a statement of principles. For UAA, the useful test is whether the campus plan mandate comes with resources.
forward_implication: Fall student listening sessions and online surveys (unscheduled as of Sept 16), then a finalized draft for approval at the November 2026 Board of Regents meeting.
